fieldEvidence.excerpt: CSE and its Cyber Centre describe an active operational requirement to help federal institutions, critical infrastructure and Canadian entities prevent, detect, assess and respond to increasingly complex cyber incidents.

Canadian government institutions and critical infrastructure face growing state-sponsored and criminal cyber threats, creating a recurring need for technical assessment, incident triage, containment advice, mitigation support and resilient digital foundations.

Reviewer synthesis of the public end state in the cited material: A resilient Canadian cyber-defence posture should identify threats quickly, coordinate response across partners, reduce disruption to essential services and provide practical technical guidance to government and critical-infrastructure operators.

fieldEvidence.excerpt: CSE identifies quantum-resistant cryptography as a capability that will define Canada's future digital security and reports briefings to prepare partners for the quantum computing threat to cryptography.
